name: C-to-U RNA Editing (APOBEC / RESCUE)
therapeuticGoalDescription: Correct pathogenic RNA sequences by recruiting or engineering cytidine deaminases (APOBEC) to catalyze cytidine-to-uridine (C→U) editing without altering genomic DNA.
molecularDefect: Pathogenic variants correctable by C→U RNA editing, where converting a mutant cytidine to uridine restores the wild-type sequence or introduces a defined change (e.g., a premature stop for targeted silencing).
diseaseMechanism: A guide RNA targets a specific cytidine within the transcript and recruits a cytidine deaminase (endogenous APOBEC or an engineered fusion such as dCas13–APOBEC / RESCUE). The deaminase converts C→U, changing the encoded codon and restoring protein function or introducing a premature stop codon.
suitableVariantTypes: T>C pathogenic variants (mutant cytidine editable to U); selected nonsense and missense mutations amenable to C→U editing; disease alleles where the wild-type base is U.
typicalDiseases: Proof-of-concept studies in monogenic disorders; RESCUE-based RNA base-editing applications; targeted silencing of gain-of-function alleles by engineered premature stop codons.
rnaTargetRegion: Target cytidine within pre-mRNA or mature mRNA, in a context that favors deaminase activity and guide-RNA binding.
transcriptRequirement: Target transcript must contain an editable cytidine within a guide-accessible region.
typicalLength: Guide RNA typically 30–120 nt (70 nt default), depending on platform and recruiting strategy.
designRules: Position the target cytidine within the deaminase activity window; optimize guide length and secondary structure; minimize bystander editing; validate editing efficiency and specificity by RNA sequencing.
secondaryStructureRequirement: Accessible RNA region permitting guide binding and deaminase recruitment; excessive secondary structure can reduce activity.
offTargetConsiderations: Bystander C→U editing; guide-RNA cross-reactivity; transcriptome-wide deamination analysis recommended.
advantages: Reversible; no permanent DNA modification; broadens the editable target space beyond adenosines.
limitations: Restricted to editable cytosines; efficiency and specificity vary by transcript and cell type; no approved therapeutic.

evidenceLevel.note: Preclinical proof-of-concept (RESCUE); clinical translation is ongoing.

referencesSummary: Abudayyeh et al. (2019); Cox et al. (2017); reviews on programmable RNA base editing.

references.paper: Abudayyeh OO et al. A cytosine deaminase for programmable single-base RNA editing (RESCUE). Science (2019)
references.usedFor: Original RESCUE platform for programmable C→U RNA editing.

references.paper: Cox DBT et al. RNA editing with CRISPR-Cas13 (REPAIR). Nature (2017)
references.usedFor: Foundational Cas13 RNA-editing platform adapted for cytidine deaminase effectors.

references.paper: Reviews on programmable RNA base editing
